shipped_rows.title_o: When ignorance is no excuse: Different roles for intent across moral domains
shipped_rows.outcome_quote: We found strong empirical support for the pattern that (1) innocent intentions induce more lenient wrongness judgements for accidentals, but weak empirical support for the pattern that (2) bad intentions induce harsher wrongness judgements for failed attempts, to a significantly larger extent for harm violations compared to purity violations. Intent plays a critical role for wrongness judgements of harm versus purity violations. Contrary to the original study, however, pattern (1) was not specific to moral judgements versus disgust ratings; and pattern (2) was not specific to moral judgements versus emotion ratings.
